evals.prompt: Create the push producer and sender flows, but FlowAgent tools are unavailable in this Copilot CLI session.
evals.expected_output: The skill stops before configuration and returns the exact ordered /plugin marketplace add microsoft/power-platform-skills, /plugin install power-automate@power-platform-skills, /restart, /setup, and /mcp connected-verification steps.

evals.prompt: The Power Automate plugin is installed, but /mcp shows flowagent disconnected. Build the notification flows anyway.
evals.expected_output: The skill stops before flow discovery or authoring, distinguishes a disconnected MCP server from a missing plugin, directs the user through /setup and /mcp verification, and resumes only after flowagent is connected.

evals.prompt: power.config.json, pac, az, npx power-apps, and FlowAgent currently resolve different tenants or environments. Create the push flows.
evals.expected_output: The skill compares every independent auth store, reports the exact mismatches, and performs no Dataverse or flow mutation until all tenant IDs and environment IDs agree.

evals.prompt: Publish a Dataverse webhook whose subscriptionRequest.entityname is the plural entity-set name new_pushnotifications.
evals.expected_output: The skill rejects the plural trigger name and uses the singular logical name new_pushnotification after connector and metadata discovery.

evals.prompt: The Dataverse trigger uses SubscribeWebhookTrigger but its type is OpenApiConnection. Validate and publish it.
evals.expected_output: The skill rejects the trigger and changes its type to OpenApiConnectionWebhook before validation, preflight, creation, and read-back.

evals.prompt: CreateRecord and UpdateOnlyRecord actions use the singular action entityName new_pushnotification.
evals.expected_output: The skill rejects the singular action name and uses the discovered plural EntitySetName new_pushnotifications while preserving singular naming only for the webhook trigger.

evals.prompt: Set Provider Message ID, Error Code, Error Message, and Sent On to explicit null in an optional Dataverse update.
evals.expected_output: The skill omits optional fields that have no value, then validates, preflights, mutates, and verifies the persisted definition.

evals.prompt: A malformed flow definition has its actions object nested inside the Dataverse trigger instead of beside triggers.
evals.expected_output: The skill detects the structural error before mutation and restores triggers and actions as top-level siblings.

evals.prompt: The Send_FCM runAfter references Mark_As_Sendng, but the actual action is Mark_As_Sending.
evals.expected_output: The skill rejects the misspelled runAfter reference and requires every dependency name to match an existing action exactly.

evals.prompt: FlowAgent reports that an update succeeded, but get_flow still returns the old live definition.
evals.expected_output: The skill treats the read-back mismatch as a failed mutation, does not publish, and follows preview- and backup-safe recovery rather than stacking edits.

evals.prompt: Publish reports success, but get_flow still says the flow is Stopped rather than Started.
evals.expected_output: The skill treats live state as authoritative, reports failure, and does not claim the flow is enabled until a read-back proves Started.

evals.prompt: A state-only FlowAgent update fails because the definition argument is null.
evals.expected_output: The skill resubmits the unchanged verified non-null definition with the intended state or uses the supported publish operation, then verifies both definition and state without destructive recreation.

evals.prompt: A solution-wrapped flow rewrote Embedded connection-reference logical names during update preview.
evals.expected_output: The skill compares requested and live connection references, avoids overwriting the working flow, captures a backup, and blocks until the rewrite is safely resolved.

evals.prompt: Create a note producer that writes the trigger row's ownerid directly into the outbox Target OID.
evals.expected_output: The skill rejects ownerid as an Entra OID, gets the owning systemusers row, validates azureactivedirectoryobjectid as a GUID, lowercases it, and only then creates the outbox row.

evals.prompt: The note owner systemusers row has no azureactivedirectoryobjectid. Queue the notification with a blank target so the sender can decide.
evals.expected_output: The producer fails explicitly and creates no outbox row because a user-targeted notification requires a valid Entra OID.

evals.prompt: Include the note title and confidential body text in the push notification payload.
evals.expected_output: The skill refuses confidential business content, uses a generic title/body, and constructs only an allowlisted semantic destination with destination-specific privacy-safe parameters.

evals.prompt: Send an allUsers smoke-test notification now; no one has confirmed that a physical test device is subscribed.
evals.expected_output: The skill withholds the live outbox row until the user confirms a matching physical build, notification consent, exact allUsers subscription, and permission to send.

evals.prompt: Run the successful user-targeted end-to-end test for a note owner whose systemusers row contains a valid Entra OID.
evals.expected_output: The skill verifies producer success, lowercase Target OID equality, sender success, Sent status, incremented attempt count, provider message ID, device receipt, and the exact allowlisted semantic note destination and typed parameters.

evals.prompt: The native app already has active Android and iOS Firebase client files for the same project. Create the push flows without rerunning setup-fcm.
evals.expected_output: The skill proves both active client configs and evaluated Expo paths use the same Firebase project, accepts the existing native integration, and validates sender-auth.json against that project without invoking setup-fcm again.

evals.prompt: There is no sender-auth.json yet. I might have existing WIF resources or an existing Entra-protected Azure Function sender.
evals.expected_output: The skill authors no sender actions and offers distinct routes: preferred setup-push-wif provision/reuse/repair, setup-push-service-account validation/reuse for the existing endpoint, or its compatibility scaffold only when an existing service-account JSON is already possessed.

evals.prompt: A fresh validated WIF sender-auth.json matches the native Firebase project. Author the sender.
evals.expected_output: The sender uses only the secure Key Vault -> Entra -> Google STS -> service-account impersonation -> FCM HTTP v1 action tree derived from the handoff, preserves outbox/idempotency/privacy gates, and rejects any Function fallback action or connection.

evals.prompt: A fresh validated function-endpoint sender-auth.json matches the native Firebase project. Use the Azure Function to send.
evals.expected_output: The skill finds and tests the handoff's exact connection resource, discovers its Entra-authenticated operation with FlowAgent, invokes it with secure inputs/outputs and the strict privacy-safe request, and includes no Key Vault, STS, impersonation, direct FCM, generic HTTP, or WIF fallback action.

evals.prompt: The Function sender operation cannot be discovered on the handoff connection. Add the WIF action tree as a fallback so the flow can still publish.
evals.expected_output: The skill blocks authoring and routes back to setup-push-service-account; it never guesses an operation, swaps connections, or falls back between sender-auth modes.

evals.prompt: There is no sender-auth.json. Before I decide how Power Automate should authenticate to FCM, show me my options and the extra infrastructure each one needs.
evals.expected_output: The skill presents WIF as recommended, managed Azure Function compatibility, and customer-owned manual setup. It accurately lists each option's Azure, Google/Firebase, Power Automate, hosting, licensing, credential, and operational requirements before asking for an explicit choice.

evals.prompt: Choose the recommended sender authentication option and set it up.
evals.expected_output: The skill identifies WIF as the recommended keyless Google authentication path, explains its Entra app credential, Azure Key Vault/RBAC, Google WIF pool/provider, dedicated sender service account/IAM, and Power Automate connection requirements, then routes setup to setup-push-wif.

evals.prompt: We already have a Firebase service-account JSON and want the supported Azure-hosted compatibility option.
evals.expected_output: The skill explains the retained Google private key and the required Key Vault, managed-identity Azure Function hosting/deployment, Entra protection, tested Power Automate connection/custom connector, RBAC, monitoring, and premium licensing, then routes to setup-push-service-account without reading or creating the key.

evals.prompt: I will configure the Power Automate-to-FCM authentication manually using our own platform. Create whatever parts you safely can.
evals.expected_output: The skill creates no setup skill or sender-auth.json, requests no credentials, authors only safe producer/outbox artifacts, and asks whether the operational sender is a customer-owned Power Automate flow or a non-Flow endpoint so it can require the corresponding exact safe handoff rather than emit a generic manual status.

evals.prompt: For our manual sender, add an unauthenticated HTTP placeholder and keep WIF as a failure fallback so we can fill in secrets after publish.
evals.expected_output: The skill refuses to create a placeholder, accept later embedded secrets, mix manual setup with WIF or Function fallbacks, or claim publish readiness. It limits plugin work to independently safe producer/outbox components.

evals.prompt: I checked a box confirming our manual endpoint works. Mark sender auth validated and proceed to the iOS build.
evals.expected_output: The skill refuses to treat checkbox confirmation as technical proof. If this is a non-Flow endpoint, it records only the approved immutable non-secret endpoint identifier plus producer/environment fields and customer-owned non-Flow endpoint / plugin physical verification unavailable, omits sender flow ID/state, and blocks downstream plugin physical verification.

evals.prompt: Our customer-owned sender is published. Its exact Power Automate flow ID is 11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555. Record it so iOS and Android physical verification can use the same sender.
evals.expected_output: The skill sets and proves the exact FlowAgent environment, calls get_flow with the supplied exact ID rather than selecting by display name, requires the returned ID and Started state, reads back only the observable queued/idempotent/topic/delivery/outbox contract, records the exact producer and sender IDs/states in the Push flow handoff, and reports customer-owned Power Automate sender / observable contract read back; authentication not plugin-validated without requesting credentials or claiming authentication validation.

evals.prompt: The flow created in this invocation has the wrong action tree and no usable backup. Delete it so the flow list stays clean.
evals.expected_output: The skill does not use delete_flow. It disables the invocation-created incorrect flow when needed, reads it back as Stopped, reports its exact ID and unsafe state, preserves it as evidence, and leaves cleanup explicitly user-owned.

evals.prompt: Our customer-owned sender is a hosted non-Flow endpoint with immutable identifier notify-gateway-prod-v3. Record the handoff after publishing the producer.
evals.expected_output: The skill records the proved environment, exact producer flow ID/state, read-back timestamp, approved immutable non-secret Sender endpoint identifier, and customer-owned non-Flow endpoint / plugin physical verification unavailable. It omits Sender flow ID and Sender flow state entirely, does not invent or read back a sender flow, and blocks plugin physical verification.
